parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State what is meant by the term *partition coefficient*.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Ammonia is soluble in both water and organic solvents.
An aqueous solution of ammonia is shaken with the immiscible organic solvent trichloromethane.
The mixture is left to reach equilibrium.

Samples are taken from each layer and titrated with dilute hydrochloric acid.

- A $25.0\text{ cm}^3$ sample from the trichloromethane layer requires $13.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.100\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{HCl}$ to reach the end-point.
- A $10.0\text{ cm}^3$ sample from the aqueous layer requires $12.5\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.100\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{HCl}$ to reach the end-point.

Calculate the partition coefficient, $K_{\text{partition}}$, of ammonia between trichloromethane and water.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
Butylamine, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{NH}_2$, is also soluble in both water and organic solvents.

Suggest how the value of $K_{\text{partition}}$ of butylamine between trichloromethane and water would compare to the value of $K_{\text{partition}}$ calculated in (ii). Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation to show butylamine reacting as a base.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: State how the basicity of butanamide, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CONH}_2$, compares to that of butylamine.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: State a reagent for the conversion of butanamide into butylamine.
